content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper tries to close the performance gap of cumbersome and lightweight contrastive models. To the end, the authors carefully tune the hyperparameters of MoCov2 and develop a variety of label smoothing in contrastive self-supervised learning.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:

The description of methods is clear.

Cons:
1. The conclusion that `the performance degeneration problem is ubiquitous in SSL methods (Sec 3.1)` is not proper.
In [1] (Figure 1), BYOL with ResNet-18 get 61.9% top-1 accuracy (800 epochs), and SwAV with ResNet-18 get 64.9% top-1 accuracy (800 epochs). In a recent paper [2], DINO with MobileNetV2 get 66.2% top-1 accuracy. The performance degeneration of small models is not so serious in these experiments, especially for SSL methods using local reviews.

2. Limited novelty and contributions. What the authors do in Table 2 is just an evolution from MoCov2 to MoCov3, e.g., cos momentum and sym loss. Why not directly use MoCov3 as the baseline? Wide MLP is discussed in Disco[3]. A modification of the label smoothing in
slef-supervised learning is not enough to make the paper an ICLR publication. Besides, the phenomenon of noisy views is discussed in 
ContrastiveCrop [5].

3. Improper baseline in Table 4. As I discussed in 2, a proper baseline should at least be MoCov3 with small models. In this case, the improvement in the performance of the method may not be significant.

4. The results are far worse than the distillation based methods. For example, two years ago, SEED[4] (Table 1) already achieves 63.0% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1k. The paper's corresponding result is 57.6.

5. In equation (1), $exp(z_i \cdot z_i^\prime / \tau)$ is summed for twice in denominator, i.e., $n \ne i$.


[1] Unsupervised Representation Transfer for Small Networks: I Believe I Can Distill On-the-Fly. https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2021/file/cecd845e3577efdaaf24eea03af4c033-Paper.pdf

[2]  EFFECTIVE SELF-SUPERVISED PRE-TRAINING ON LOW-COMPUTE NETWORKS WITHOUT DISTILLATION. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2210.02808.pdf

[3] Yuting Gao, Jia-Xin Zhuang, Ke Li, Hao Cheng, Xiaowei Guo, Feiyue Huang, Rongrong Ji, and
Xing Sun. Disco: Remedy self-supervised learning on lightweight models with distilled contrastive
learning. arXiv preprint arXiv:2104.09124, 2021.

[4] Zhiyuan Fang, Jianfeng Wang, Lijuan Wang, Lei Zhang, Yezhou Yang, and Zicheng Liu. Seed:
Self-supervised distillation for visual representation. In International Conference on Learning
Representations, 2020.

[5] Crafting Better Contrastive Views for Siamese Representation Learning. CVPR 2022. https://github.com/xyupeng/ContrastiveCrop

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focuses on self-supervised contrastive learning of lightweight models. Specifically, this paper utilizes a bag of training techniques and a softened NCE loss to improve the performance of these models. The experiments show that, by adopting the bag of training techniques, the performance can be improved by a large margin on top of MoCo v2 for several lightweight models (e.g., Resnet18).
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strength
1. It identifies the gap on lightweight models between contrastive learning and supervised training.
2. It provides an extensive ablation study of different training techniques on Resnet-18, which could be useful for other researchers.
2. The proposed label smoothing version of NCE loss is well motivated.

## Weaknesses
1. In my understanding, this paper is trying to bridge the gap between training a lightweight model using contrastive learning and training the same model by supervised training. If this is correct, then the current title (and those sentences supporting this title) is quite misleading which suggests, for example, it can bridge the performance gap between a Resnet-18 and a Resnet-50 (trained using similar techniques) which is not likely to hold.
2. This paper is quite limited in terms of novelty. It is more about assembling existing techniques to do contrastive learning properly. 
3. From the experimental perspective, Table 4 (classification) only contains one baseline method which is not enough given so many recent works on contrastive learning. Table 4 also lacks necessary ablation study. The improvement in Table 5 (object detection) is marginal, thus it requires some confidence interval to justify the significance.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Quality is reasonable.
Clarity is ok (title may need changes).
Novelty is limited.
content.summary_of_the_review: The direction of training lightweight model under the contrastive learning framework is worth pursuing, while the novelty of this paper is limited and the current experimental results are not enough to prove that the proposed bag of techniques can boost the performance of contrastive learning evaluated on different tasks.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper revisits the problem of training self-supervised lightweight models. Instead of distilling the small models with a larger self-supervised trained teacher model, this work aims at improving the self-supervised method itself to better adapt to small models. Training hyper-parameters are tuned and the original InfoNCE loss used in MoCo v2 is revised as a softened one. Performances of small models are finally promoted without an additional distillation process.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strength**    
This paper reveals a valuable comment that current self-supervised learning methods can do more on small/tiny models. Though most conclusions/contributions are based on experimental studies, these clues are still expected to benefit this field. If the code is released, it would be a good baseline for other researchers/engineers to try more with small models.

**Weaknesses**   
* One point I may not agree with lies in the opinion that distillation introduces huge cost for pretraining a large teacher model. As is known, the teacher model pretraining usually acts once for all. Besides, the community has released many self-supervised pre-trained models which can be directly used as the teacher. In previous methods, the teacher is usually a plain one which does not need any special treatment. I think the cost brought by teacher models is somewhat over-claimed by this paper. Anyway, this point does not affect its contribution to improving self-supervised learning methods themselves.
* It has been claimed as a limitation that the approach has not yet been explored with other methods beyond MoCo-v2. However, I still concern about how much impact this method will cause which is only adapted to MoCo-v2. Many MIM (masked image modeling) methods have emerged with higher accuracy and efficiency, which may be more commonly used nowadays.
* I wonder whether the adopted techniques will take effect on large models.
* Though distillation-based methods may take larger cost, they, e.g. BINGO, DISCO, should still be compared in the experiment tables where training cost can be also included as a comparison item.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
* **Clarity**: Most contents are clear and easy to follow.
* **Quality**: The proposed method has been evaluated and studied on some important benchmarks and settings. However, some comparisons are still needed as mentioned in the weaknesses.
* **Novelty**: Most techniques come from previous works or experimental searching/trials. The novelty may lie more in the problem itself.
* **Reproducibility**: Most implementation details and the code are provided. It is likely to reproduce the method.
content.summary_of_the_review: I have listed some concerns regarding claims on distillation, its impact, and experimental soundness. These are expected to be resolved in the response. Anyway, the overall idea of improving the SSL methods on small models is good and may give inspiration to this community.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
*I am an emergency reviewer.*

This paper studies the problem of self-supervised training of (relatively) small deep models. The first set of experiments is trying several contrastive learning methods on ResNet-18, reporting significantly lower performance. The second set of experiments is tuning hyperparameters for ResNet-18 and EfficientNet-B0, showing that a larger MLP head is quite useful for EfficientNet-B0. The third observation is that false contrastive pairs may be the root cause of low performance. So authors introduce the label smoothing trick into infoNCE, reporting further improved performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
+ Clearly written, nice figures.
+ Significant results on ImageNet.

Weaknesses:
- The first issue is limited technical contribution. Doing this kind of research needs a minimal amount of code development or mathematical analysis. So the primary consideration is whether the insights are conclusive or useful.
- W.r.t. the first set of experiments, I guess more compact backbones need to be analyzed? If SimSiam also performs the worst for MobileNet  or EfficientNet, that may lead to some interesting conclusions if well analyzed. But for now, I draw no clear conclusions from Table.1
- W.r.t. the second set of experiments, the only interesting thing I see is a wider MLP brings sifnificant margins for EfficientNet-B0. I am not sure what this means. Maybe this difference comes from the usage of depth-wise convolution. If so, I guess authors should tune MLP width for MobileNet too.
- W.r.t. the smoothed infoNCE, I think this can be considered a technical contribution to some extent, considering the challenges of 65536 classes in MOCO. However, the insight is that the smoothed version can be used to address the false contrastive pair problem. If so, it should work for large models too? Correct me if I am wrong.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: Reading this paper is quite a pleasure.
Quality: Well executed.
Novelty: Limited technical novelty and somewhat significant empirical novelty.
Reproducibility: Should be easy to implement.
content.summary_of_the_review: I am open-minded to this kind of bag-of-tricks papers if clear conclusions can be drawn. But for this version, I have concerns as stated in the Weakness part.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a bag of tricks that makes the MoCo-v2 works better with small network architectures. Concretely, the authors fine-tuned hyper-parameters, and employ the InfoNCE with a soft target to overcome the noisy label during training. In the experimental analysis, the authours boost the baseline performance by a large margin.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

The experimental results are fairly good and promising compared to the baseline, the experience reported in this paper should be useful in explaining the deeper mechanism behind self-contrastive learning.

Weaknesses:

The contribution of this paper is not significant in my opinion, it demonstrates a lot of tricks that work but does not explain why these tricks work in-depth, it feels like a technical report, and may not be helpful in my only cases. Also, I doubt if these conclusions are heavily related to other factors such as batch size, data augmentation, and datasets employed.

The idea of InfoNCE with a soft target is also not novel. The major difference between this work and formerly published works is how the hard samples are defined and how the target should be smoothed. I don't say this part is out of any novelty, but it is not solid and significant. Perhaps the authors could conduct experiments on different soft target InfoNCE algorithms and provide a comparison.

In practice, it is not a problem to employ a distillation-based method to learn a small model that is actually deployed on an edge device. Therefore, I somewhat wonder about the practical value of this work, though it still provides a lot of information on this topic. Perhaps the authors could provide more comparisons of performance with the distillation-based methods (not only the SEED, but more standard distillation methods).

The connection between Section 3 and Section 4 is not clear, I have no idea if Section 3 is related to the major contribution of this paper. In my opinion this section should be put to appendix.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is well-written and easy to follow.

Quality: The overall quality is moderate due to the weaknesses mentioned above.

Novelty: The overall novelty is limited.

Reproducibility: This paper might be hard to reproduce since many hyper-parameters are induced and tuned.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper could not meet the acceptance bar without a more in-depth technical analysis.
